segments.text: The closest planet outside our solar system is right next door. Could you live there?
The nearest star to the Sun is a small red dwarf called Proxima Centauri.
segments.headline: Our nearest star

segments.text: It's four point two light-years away. About forty trillion kilometers.
It's so faint you can't see it without a telescope, even though it's our closest neighbor.

visual.query: Milky Way southern sky Alpha Centauri
visual.commons: Milky Way southern sky Alpha Centauri

segments.headline: Too faint to see

segments.text: In twenty sixteen, astronomers found a planet orbiting it, a bit heavier than Earth. They named it Proxima b.
segments.headline: Proxima b, 2016

segments.text: It circles its star every eleven days, at a distance where liquid water could exist on the surface.
But there's a problem. Proxima Centauri throws violent flares, blasting the planet with radiation that could strip away its air.
segments.headline: Violent flares

segments.text: The planet is probably tidally locked: one side always faces the star, the other is in endless night.
segments.headline: Endless day, endless night

segments.text: Could life survive there? Maybe on the line between day and night. Or under the surface. We don't know yet.
